title: Why You Keep Checking If They Replied
header: Why you keep checking if they replied
description:
Why do you keep checking if they replied? It isn't neediness. Your brain is fighting uncertainty. In a University College London study, a fifty-fifty chance of an electric shock was more stressful than knowing a shock was certain. Here's why every check feels like a slot machine, and one simple way to break the loop.

Follow The Human Side for more on the things we feel but rarely talk about.
source: de Berker et al. (2016), Computations of uncertainty mediate acute stress responses in humans, Nature Communications

scenes.text: You've checked if they replied... how many times now?
In one study, people faced a fifty-fifty chance of an electric shock.
That stressed them more than knowing for sure it was coming.
For your brain, not knowing can feel worse than bad news.
So every check feels like it might pay off. Like a slot machine.
Try this: put your phone in another room for twenty minutes.
The reply won't come faster because you're watching.
And now you're wondering if they've replied.
